title: CRL cache rollback accepts any CRL lacking cRLNumber; the OCSP side would not
description:
## What

`pkix-revocation-http`'s `is_rollback` (cache.rs:896) refuses an incoming
CRL only when the cached one carries a `cRLNumber` greater than the
incoming one:

    (Some(p), Some(inc)) => match p.crl_number() {
        Some(prior_num) => crl_number_gt(prior_num, inc),
        None => false,
    },
    _ => false,

So whenever *either* side lacks the extension the answer is "not a
rollback", and the incoming CRL displaces whatever is cached -- including
a higher-numbered one.

## Why it looks like an unmade decision rather than a considered one

The OCSP half of the same cache does have a fallback comparator, and it
is exactly the one the CRL half does not use:

    fn is_staler_ocsp(prior, incoming_this_update) -> bool {
        Some(p) => p.this_update() > incoming_this_update,
        None => false,
    }

And `CachedCrl::this_update` is already parsed, stored and public
(cache.rs:215, `tbsCertList.thisUpdate`) -- and verified today to feed no
decision anywhere in the crate. Every `this_update()` call site is the
OCSP path. So the comparator the CRL side would need is sitting there
unused, while the OCSP side uses its twin.

## How reachable

RFC 5280 §5.2.3 says conforming CRL issuers MUST include `cRLNumber`, so
this needs a non-conforming issuer, or a truncated/retagged extension
that fails to parse. That makes it low-likelihood rather than
unreachable, and the consequence is a cache that can be walked backwards
by whoever controls the distribution point: serve a stale CRL with no
`cRLNumber` and the fresher cached one is gone.

## The decision this needs

Three options, and picking one is a maintainer's call rather than a test
gap:

1. Fall back to `thisUpdate` when either side lacks `cRLNumber`, making
   the two halves of the cache symmetric and giving the already-parsed
   field a purpose.
2. Refuse to cache a CRL with no `cRLNumber` at all, on the grounds that
   §5.2.3 requires it and an issuer omitting it has given the cache
   nothing to order by.
3. Keep the present behaviour and say in the rustdoc that ordering
   depends on `cRLNumber` and a CRL without one always wins, so a caller
   knows what it is getting.

Option 1 is the smallest change and the most consistent; option 2 is the
most conservative. Either way the asymmetry with `is_staler_ocsp` should
stop being silent.

## Found by

The pkix-revocation-http mutation sweep, 2026-11-27, which closed all 25
of that crate's survivors. This is not one of them -- no mutation
exposes it, because the behaviour is intended as written. It surfaced
from reading the two comparators side by side.
